newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania firm agrees to settle SEC fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania firm agrees to settle SEC fraud charges.

text.p: Healthcare Services Group Inc. has agreed to settle fraud and other charges in connection with a $22 million public stock offering in 1990, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday.
Under the proposed settlement, the Huntingdon Valley, Pa.-based supplier of laundry, linen and other services to hospitals will be required to pay a civil penalty of $650,000, the SEC said.

Three others charged in the case, former chairman Daniel McCartney, former marketing vice president Melvyn Mason and former chief financial officer and current president Thomas Cook will be required to pay monetary penalties totalling $200,000, it said.
In addition, Mason will be barred from serving as an officer or director of any public company for seven years. All the defendants will be enjoined from further violating federal securities laws.
The defendants have consented to the settlement without admitting or denying any wrongdoing, the SEC said. The three could not be immediately reached for comment.

In a civil complaint filed in federal court in Philadelphia, the SEC alleged that Healthcare, McCartney and Cook failed to adequately disclose in the company's stock offering "material risk" that clients accounting for about 35 percent of its revenues would cancel their contracts.
Those contracts were related to service agreements of American Services Co., a Southmark Corp. subsidiary that Healthcare bought in 1988.

The SEC also charged the company with filing false and misleading financial statements in 1990 and 1991 arising from a variety of accounting failures. In addition, it alleged that Healthcare and Mason failed to disclose that the company paid certain third parties $400,000 between 1988 and 1991 for no valid business purposes.
A federal court in Philadelphia, where the SEC filed its civil complaint, is scheduled to hold a hearing on Oct. 15 to consider the proposed settlement, the agency said.
